capabilities.name: Device and Windows readiness summary
capabilities.outcome: A user can understand the device's core hardware and Windows characteristics and whether they are suitable for endpoint-management assessment.
capabilities.rationale: Preserve the legacy device overview while replacing raw command dumps with normalized readiness evidence and interpretation.

capabilities.name: Windows edition, activation, and licensing readiness
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify Windows edition, build, activation state, and relevant entitlement readiness without exposing product keys.
capabilities.rationale: Keep the readiness outcome but replace broad licensing dumps and embedded-key disclosure with a minimal, privacy-safe state assessment.

capabilities.name: Firmware and TPM readiness assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can understand BIOS and TPM availability and relevant readiness limitations for endpoint security and management.
capabilities.rationale: Retain BIOS and TPM observation while adding explicit interpretation, unavailable states, and virtual-versus-physical evidence limits.

capabilities.name: Device form, virtualization, and power context
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify physical or virtual device context, portable form factor, and available battery evidence when those facts affect assessment conclusions.
capabilities.rationale: Combine related device-form observations into one outcome while preserving that physical hardware claims require representative physical evidence.

capabilities.name: Device registration and join assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can determine the device's Microsoft Entra and domain registration state and understand material enrollment-readiness findings.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: main/Device Registration Troubleshooter Command Tool
capabilities.rationale: Preserve the core Intune-project discovery outcome while replacing unstructured dsreg output with normalized evidence and findings.

capabilities.name: Work or school account and enrollment context
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify relevant local work or school account context needed to investigate enrollment without treating account identifiers as public evidence.
capabilities.rationale: Retain locally useful enrollment context while classifying account identifiers as sensitive and preventing them from entering public artifacts by default.

capabilities.name: Local administrator exposure assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can understand local administrator membership and material privilege-risk findings on the assessed device.
capabilities.rationale: Preserve privileged-membership discovery while adding risk interpretation and handling account names as sensitive evidence.

capabilities.name: Effective management policy assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify relevant effective local and domain policy state and understand how it may affect endpoint-management readiness.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: main/Group and Local Policies Information
capabilities.rationale: Retain policy discovery but replace fragile text scraping with structured evidence, explicit limitations, and interpretation.

capabilities.name: Software and application migration inventory
capabilities.outcome: A user can review installed desktop and packaged applications and identify migration-relevant facts without triggering installer repair or reconfiguration.
capabilities.rationale: Preserve software inventory while replacing the unsafe Win32_Product path with side-effect-safe sources and explicit completeness states.

capabilities.name: User resource and peripheral dependency inventory
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify shared folders, mapped drives, and printers that may require migration planning.
capabilities.rationale: Group related user-resource dependencies into a migration outcome and distinguish absent, inaccessible, partial, and complete evidence.

capabilities.name: Network adapter and connection readiness
capabilities.outcome: A user can understand active network adapters and connection profiles relevant to management-service reachability.
capabilities.rationale: Retain network context while minimizing identifiers and separating configuration evidence from active connectivity tests.

capabilities.name: Microsoft management and security service connectivity
capabilities.outcome: A user can test scenario-relevant Microsoft management and security endpoints and distinguish DNS, transport, policy, and service failures.
capabilities.rationale: Replace a static, broad endpoint sweep with versioned scenario catalogs, bounded tests, and actionable failure classification.

capabilities.name: Enterprise enrollment and registration DNS assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can compare expected enterprise enrollment and registration name resolution with the device's configured resolver behavior.
capabilities.rationale: Preserve comparative DNS diagnosis while making resolver choice, active network activity, and sensitive domain handling explicit.

capabilities.name: Certificate and trust readiness assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user can identify certificate and local trust conditions that materially affect enrollment, management, or service connectivity.
capabilities.rationale: The v2 baseline recognizes certificates and trust as an outcome area even though the legacy script has no coherent certificate-readiness result.

capabilities.name: Controlled Assessment Run
capabilities.outcome: An operator can preflight, consent to, scope, execute, observe, and complete one assessment with explicit privileges, side effects, and completion state.
capabilities.rationale: Replace the monolithic elevated script flow with a bounded Assessment Run whose consent, privilege, progress, cancellation, cleanup, and outcome are observable.

capabilities.name: Scoped user and system-context assessment
capabilities.outcome: An operator can run only approved checks in the user or local-system context required by the selected scenario and see which context produced each result.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: main/Tests to Intune and Defender for Endpoint network Endpoints
capabilities.rationale: Keep context-sensitive diagnosis but replace arbitrary scheduled-task execution with narrow, declared, auditable context transitions.

capabilities.name: Explicit incomplete and failure outcomes
capabilities.outcome: A user can distinguish successful, partial, unavailable, not-applicable, denied, timed-out, cancelled, and failed assessment results.
capabilities.rationale: Legacy empty files, caught errors, and skipped checks can resemble success; v2 requires first-class outcome states.

capabilities.name: Versioned assessment evidence package
capabilities.outcome: A user receives one versioned local evidence package with provenance, completeness, schema, and sensitivity metadata.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: generated Config, Network, Software, account, endpoint, and Battery outputs
capabilities.rationale: Replace many timestamped raw files with a coherent, versioned package that records provenance and incomplete collection honestly.

capabilities.name: Findings and recommendations report
capabilities.outcome: A user receives an understandable report that separates observations from interpreted findings, limitations, and advisory next steps.
capabilities.rationale: The legacy script gathers data but does not provide a versioned observation-to-finding contract or clearly advisory guidance.

capabilities.name: Privacy-minimized local evidence handling
capabilities.outcome: A user can assess a device while collection, storage, display, and sharing defaults minimize sensitive evidence and prohibit automatic telemetry.
capabilities.rationale: Broad legacy collection includes identity, network, licensing, and credential-sensitive evidence; every public build needs safe defaults and local control.

capabilities.name: Safe public feedback bundle
capabilities.outcome: A user can intentionally create and locally preview a redacted diagnostic bundle suitable for a public defect report without including raw assessment evidence by default.
capabilities.rationale: Public feedback must be possible without normalizing attachment of raw logs or complete assessment packages.

capabilities.name: Beginner-friendly public product documentation
capabilities.outcome: A beginner can safely start, understand terminology and results, and progressively reach deeper operational and troubleshooting guidance without a separate handoff.
capabilities.rationale: Public documentation is part of the product and must teach while remaining useful to experienced testers and consultants.

capabilities.name: Language-neutral execution and basic primary-path operability
capabilities.outcome: A user can complete the English interface's primary assessment path on a supported Windows display language or locale while evidence and automation remain Unicode-safe and culture-independent.
capabilities.rationale: The existing compound identity retains its compatible mandatory core: the English interface must run safely across supported Windows languages and locales, preserve Unicode, avoid translated-text parsing, and keep the primary path keyboard-operable; formal accessibility receives a separate identity and later obligation.

capabilities.name: Portable public distribution and first-run experience
capabilities.outcome: A user with an externally installed eligible stable PowerShell 7.6-or-later 7.x runtime can obtain, verify, and start WIN-PCInfo from a documented portable distribution; an ineligible or missing runtime ends safely with installation and retry guidance and no runtime change by WIN-PCInfo.
capabilities.rationale: Retain portable download-and-run use while making PowerShell an explicit external prerequisite: a Windows PowerShell bootstrap may only detect and relaunch an eligible host or provide retry guidance, and WIN-PCInfo never changes the runtime or bypasses execution policy; an installer or compiled launcher remains a later decision.

capabilities.name: Trusted release provenance and integrity
capabilities.outcome: A user can independently verify publisher identity or the approved preview fallback, source revision, modular-source and deterministic-build provenance, the exact generated application, authenticated supporting resources, dependency inventory, and artifact integrity.
capabilities.rationale: Preview may use explicit unsigned attestation, but Stable 2.0.0 requires trusted Authenticode signing; every public artifact requires verifiable provenance, and the authentic primary application must authenticate every governing supporting resource before use.

capabilities.name: Preview capability and support transparency
capabilities.outcome: A user can see which capabilities and scenarios are available, limited, experimental, deferred, or not yet supported for a specific release.
capabilities.rationale: Public previews are advisory and must not imply support beyond their frozen ledger snapshot and recorded evidence.

capabilities.name: Evidence-gated release promotion
capabilities.outcome: The maintainer can publish or promote a release only when every universal gate and every automated, client, community, security, provenance, and supported-scenario evidence source applicable to its actual claims is complete.
capabilities.rationale: Release maturity is an evidence threshold, not merely an implementation or version label. Community Validation is checked only for a claim whose material behavior controlled Client VM Validation cannot credibly establish, so its complete workflow is not forced into every Preview slice or promotion.

capabilities.name: Fresh Azure Client VM Validation rounds
capabilities.outcome: The maintainer can run bounded validation on one to four fresh private Windows client VMs and finish with sanitized evidence and no round-created Azure residue.
capabilities.rationale: Windows-client behavior unavailable on Server CI needs fresh official evaluation clients, private networking, strict cost and lifetime limits, and verified teardown after every round.

capabilities.name: Privacy-preserving Community Validation Runs
capabilities.outcome: When a claimed scenario cannot be established credibly in the controlled Azure lab, a tester can contribute version-linked, scenario-specific validation evidence without publishing restricted device, person, tenant, organization, or network data.
capabilities.rationale: Representative physical and externally managed scenarios cannot all be established by virtual infrastructure, but their evidence must remain privacy-safe. Stable-required means this workflow is available by Stable 2.0.0; it does not make Community Validation mandatory for every scenario, promotion, or Preview slice.

capabilities.name: Automated deterministic release gates
capabilities.outcome: The maintainer can repeatably validate deterministic logic, schemas, fixtures, modular-source and generated-artifact equivalence, authenticated package resources, secret prevention, and eligible-runtime compatibility before publishing.
capabilities.rationale: Deterministic release properties, exact runtime and validator qualification, and the equivalence of modular source to the generated candidate belong in automated gates; client-only and physical scenarios remain separate evidence paths.

capabilities.name: Governance, contribution, and maintenance transparency
capabilities.outcome: A contributor or user can understand maintainer authority, MIT and DCO terms, review and security channels, triage, deprecation, and best-effort maintenance limits.
capabilities.rationale: The public project must communicate realistic authority and maintenance boundaries without promising support timelines.

capabilities.name: Privacy-preserving adoption and outcome measures
capabilities.outcome: The maintainer can learn whether the product is being tried and useful through intentional privacy-safe signals rather than automatic telemetry.
capabilities.rationale: The measurement contract is in scope but deliberately awaits its governing decision; automatic telemetry remains prohibited.

capabilities.name: Clear-text wireless credential export
capabilities.outcome: The product would export saved wireless profiles together with clear-text keys.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: main/Networking details, netsh wlan export profile key=clear
capabilities.rationale: Exporting recoverable wireless credentials is unnecessary for readiness assessment and creates unacceptable secret-disclosure risk.

capabilities.name: Firmware-embedded product key disclosure
capabilities.outcome: The product would write a firmware-embedded Windows product key into assessment output.
capabilities.rationale: Readiness needs activation and entitlement state, not disclosure of a recoverable license key.

capabilities.name: Device remediation, fleet management, and tenant-wide collection
capabilities.outcome: The product would change device state, administer a fleet, or collect evidence across a tenant rather than assess one local client.
capabilities.rationale: WIN-PCInfo v2 assesses one local Windows client; remediation, fleet administration, and tenant-wide collection are separate products with different risks.

capabilities.name: Windows Server assessment
capabilities.outcome: A user would receive assessment claims for Windows Server devices.
capabilities.rationale: Windows Server runners are useful for deterministic gates but are not an assessed-device target for WIN-PCInfo v2.

capabilities.name: Automatic product telemetry
capabilities.outcome: The product would automatically transmit usage, device, or assessment signals to the maintainer.
capabilities.rationale: Automatic telemetry is outside the product boundary; any adoption signal must be intentional and privacy-preserving.

capabilities.name: Built-in private diagnostic upload
capabilities.outcome: The product would upload restricted diagnostic or assessment evidence to a project-operated private service.
capabilities.rationale: The project will use public privacy-safe feedback paths and will not operate a private evidence ingestion service.

capabilities.name: Formal accessibility conformance
capabilities.outcome: A user would receive a formally defined and validated accessibility experience beyond the mandatory Language-neutral Execution and Basic Primary-path Operability baseline.
capabilities.rationale: Formal WCAG, WCAG2ICT, assistive-technology, or comparable conformance is intentionally distinct from the mandatory cross-locale and basic keyboard-operability baseline, and no formal conformance target is required for v2 Preview or Stable publication.

components.name: Device and OS inventory collector
components.purpose: Collect normalized hardware, manufacturer, model, processor, memory, Windows edition, build, and architecture evidence without broad raw object dumps.

components.name: Windows activation and entitlement-state collector
components.purpose: Collect the minimum activation, edition, and licensing-state evidence needed for readiness while excluding product keys.

components.name: Firmware and TPM collector
components.purpose: Collect BIOS and TPM availability, version, and status evidence with explicit unavailable and access-denied states.

components.name: Form-factor, virtualization, and power collector
components.purpose: Collect device form, virtualization context, chassis, battery presence, and bounded power evidence relevant to result interpretation.

components.name: Device registration-state collector
components.purpose: Collect structured Microsoft Entra and domain registration evidence with source context and explicit collection status.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: main/Device Registration Troubleshooter Command Tool

components.name: Work or school account context collector
components.purpose: Collect only the local work or school account context required for enrollment assessment and classify identifiers as sensitive.

components.name: Local privileged-membership collector
components.purpose: Collect local Administrators-group membership using locale-safe identity and group identifiers with access and completeness status.

components.name: Effective policy collector
components.purpose: Collect structured effective local and domain policy evidence without relying on localized report text scraping.

components.name: Side-effect-safe software inventory collector
components.purpose: Collect installed desktop and packaged application evidence from sources that do not invoke Windows Installer consistency checks or repairs.

components.name: User resource and peripheral collector
components.purpose: Collect mapped drives, shared folders, and printer dependencies with per-source access and completeness state.

components.name: Network configuration collector
components.purpose: Collect bounded adapter, connection-profile, route, and resolver context while minimizing device and network identifiers.

components.name: Microsoft service connectivity collector
components.purpose: Perform declared, bounded DNS and transport checks against endpoints selected by the assessment scenario and catalog version.

components.name: Enrollment DNS collector
components.purpose: Resolve enterprise enrollment and registration names through declared configured or comparison resolvers and retain response provenance.

components.name: Certificate and trust collector
components.purpose: Collect bounded local certificate and trust evidence required by a selected enrollment, management, or connectivity scenario.

components.name: Device readiness interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret device, Windows, form-factor, virtualization, and power observations into evidence-bounded readiness states and limitations.

components.name: Windows activation and edition interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret Windows edition, build, and activation evidence without presenting license keys or making legal-entitlement claims.

components.name: Firmware security readiness interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret BIOS and TPM evidence according to scenario and distinguish virtual evidence from claims requiring physical validation.

components.name: Identity and enrollment interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret device registration, account context, and enrollment DNS evidence into scenario-specific findings without inferring success from missing data.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: Device Registration and Azure AD account sections

components.name: Privileged account risk interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret local privileged membership with source, completeness, expected-account, and evidence-sensitivity context.

components.name: Policy posture interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret collected effective policy evidence into management-readiness findings while retaining unknown and inaccessible states.

components.name: Application migration interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret application, drive, share, and printer evidence into migration-relevant inventory states and advisory follow-up.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: software, share, drive, and printer collectors

components.name: Connectivity and DNS interpretation
components.purpose: Distinguish local configuration, DNS, transport, egress-policy, endpoint-catalog, and remote-service causes without treating every failure as device incompatibility.

components.name: Certificate and trust interpretation
components.purpose: Interpret certificate presence, validity, chain, and trust observations only within the declared assessment scenario.

components.name: Evidence completeness and outcome-state rule
components.purpose: Assign explicit success, partial, unavailable, not-applicable, denied, timed-out, cancelled, and failed states to observations and aggregate outcomes.

components.name: Findings and recommendations report
components.purpose: Present observations, findings, limitations, advisory recommendations, and next steps in a readable versioned report.

components.name: Versioned assessment evidence package
components.purpose: Store normalized evidence, collection status, provenance, sensitivity metadata, and schema version in one bounded local package.

components.name: Assessment manifest
components.purpose: Record tool and schema versions, source revision, selected profile, collection outcome summary, package contents, and integrity data.

components.name: Redacted feedback bundle
components.purpose: Produce a separately generated, locally previewable diagnostic archive that excludes raw logs and complete assessment packages by default.

components.name: Release manifest
components.purpose: Record release identity, source revision, ledger schema and hash, exact generated-application and supporting-resource digests, exact tested runtime, validator, dependency, and architecture identities, deterministic-build provenance, and applicable evidence references.

components.name: Preview capability matrix
components.purpose: Publish version-specific capability and scenario states derived from the frozen ledger and approved support evidence.

components.name: Assessment Run lifecycle
components.purpose: Coordinate preflight, consent, collection, progress, cancellation, cleanup, completion, and exit behavior for one Assessment Run.

components.name: Execution-profile selection workflow
components.purpose: Let an operator select a declared assessment scope whose collectors, contexts, privilege, network activity, and side effects are known before execution.

components.name: User and local-system context workflow
components.purpose: Run only predefined checks in their required local context and attach context provenance to every result.
sourceReferences: ComputerInfo.ps1: user and SYSTEM endpoint tests

components.name: Public feedback and contribution workflow
components.purpose: Route questions, ideas, defects, changes, and security reports to the approved public or private channel with privacy and DCO boundaries.

components.name: Portable package and first-run workflow
components.purpose: Guide acquisition, integrity verification, the external stable PowerShell 7.6-or-later 7.x prerequisite, Windows PowerShell detection and relaunch, the Runtime Compatibility Check, first launch, and safe installation-and-retry guidance without WIN-PCInfo installing or changing the runtime.

components.name: Trusted signing and preview attestation workflow
components.purpose: Apply trusted Authenticode signing when available and the explicitly warned provenance attestation fallback only to eligible Preview Releases.

components.name: Automated Gate workflow
components.purpose: Run deterministic logic, fixture, schema-validator conformance, packaging, static, secret-prevention, Runtime Compatibility Check, modular-source-to-generated-artifact equivalence, authenticated-resource, and exact runtime and architecture checks on ephemeral automation workers.

components.name: Client VM Validation workflow
components.purpose: Exercise client-only installation, launch, collection, cancellation, cleanup, reporting, update, and upgrade behavior on a fresh private Windows client VM.

components.name: Community Validation workflow
components.purpose: Collect intentional, version-linked, scenario-declared, privacy-sanitized validation attestations only when a claimed behavior cannot be established credibly through controlled Client VM Validation.

components.name: Language-neutral and basic-operability interaction workflow
components.purpose: Present the English primary path with understandable keyboard-operable controls, visible focus, no keyboard traps or color-only meaning, while preserving Unicode and avoiding interpretation of localized Windows display text.

components.name: Versioned Microsoft endpoint catalog
components.purpose: Provide maintained, scenario-specific endpoint and DNS expectations with source, version, applicability, and retirement metadata.

components.name: Capability ledger and release snapshot catalog
components.purpose: Supply the canonical capability inventory and immutable release-specific ledger snapshot used for matrices, gates, and manifests.

components.name: Approved Azure evaluation gallery catalog
components.purpose: Identify approved pristine Windows 10 and Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation gallery versions and their source-integrity, security, lifecycle, and retirement status.

components.name: Validation egress profile catalog
components.purpose: Define versioned restricted scenario profiles and the explicitly selected temporary Full Outbound diagnostic profile for Validation Rounds.

components.name: Consent, scope, and privilege gate
components.purpose: Block collection or context elevation until the operator can review and approve the declared scope, privileges, network activity, side effects, and outputs.

components.name: Cancellation, timeout, cleanup, and honest-completion control
components.purpose: Bound execution, stop safely, remove temporary state, and prevent cancelled, timed-out, failed, or incomplete work from appearing successful.

components.name: Evidence minimization and redaction control
components.purpose: Classify, minimize, segregate, preview, and redact sensitive evidence before it can enter a sharing artifact or public validation record.

components.name: Supply-chain provenance and integrity control
components.purpose: Bind modular source, exact runtime and dependencies, deterministic build process, generated application, authenticated supporting resources, signatures or attestations, and release metadata and block every integrity or provenance failure.

components.name: Release evidence and support promotion gate
components.purpose: Block publication or support promotion unless every universal obligation and every approved automated, client, community, security, and provenance evidence source applicable to the actual claim is satisfied; Community Validation is conditional by scenario.

components.name: Azure round budget, concurrency, and teardown control
components.purpose: Enforce budget readiness, one active round, one to four allowlisted small Standard-SSD VMs, a six-hour maximum, cleanup-first cancellation, and zero residue before another round.

components.name: Credentialless validation identity and network-boundary control
components.purpose: Use the least-privilege host managed identity to create and remove round resources and non-transitive host peering while failing closed when the approved host-network invariant is not true.

components.name: Automatic telemetry prohibition
components.purpose: Prevent automatic transmission of product usage, device, or assessment data and require intentional privacy-safe feedback paths.

components.name: Fresh evaluation-client control
components.purpose: Require each validation VM to come from a pristine approved gallery baseline, prohibit capture or reuse after testing, prohibit rearm, and require destruction after its single round.

components.name: Beginner product documentation
components.purpose: Teach terminology, purpose, prerequisites, safe procedures, expected outcomes, limitations, troubleshooting, and next steps through progressive disclosure.

components.name: Privacy and safe-sharing documentation
components.purpose: Teach evidence sensitivity, local preview and redaction, prohibited public content, safe feedback paths, and cleanup expectations.

components.name: Release status and capability documentation
components.purpose: Explain Preview and Stable status, signatures or attestation, capability matrices, scenario support, limitations, deprecation, and evidence provenance.

components.name: Governance, contribution, and maintenance documentation
components.purpose: Explain maintainer authority, MIT and DCO terms, required checks, contribution and security channels, triage, release maintenance, deprecation, and absence of service commitments.

components.name: Validation operator documentation
components.purpose: Teach safe automated, Client VM, and Community Validation procedures, licensing boundaries, evidence handling, cost and concurrency controls, and verified teardown.

components.name: Formal accessibility validation workflow
components.purpose: Define and validate a future formal accessibility target, including its applicable conformance criteria, assistive-technology coverage, evidence, and public claim language, beyond the mandatory basic-operability baseline.
